papers.title_in_file: Digital-analog quantum learning on Rydberg atom arrays
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2401.02940v2 (9 May 2025); matches the record's title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, noise model and gate fidelity section, digit classification results, phase boundary learning results, conclusion and outlook. Appendices skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of hybrid digital-analog variational learning circuits for Rydberg atom arrays, tested on handwritten digit classification and unsupervised quantum phase boundary learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that their construction requires only single-qubit operations in the digital setting and global driving according to the Rydberg Hamiltonian in the analog setting.
quotes: Our construction requires only single-qubit operations in the digital setting and global driving according to the Rydberg Hamiltonian in the analog setting.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' statement of their own construction, Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors report, from a numerical study on two representative problems, that digital-analog learning is feasible in the near term, requires shorter circuit depths and is more robust to realistic error models than digital learning schemes.
quotes: We show in the two representative problems that digital-analog learning is not only feasible in the near term, but also requires shorter circuit depths and is more robust to realistic error models as compared to digital learning schemes.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical simulation in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The evidence is simulation with an assumed noise model, not hardware runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that the noise-robustness advantage of digital-analog circuits in phase boundary learning is lost if the choice of hyperparameter with respect to noise is poor.
assertions.anchor: Section III phase boundary learning, p.14-15
quotes: We observe, however, that this advantage is lost if the choice of hyperparameter with respect to noise is poor, as shown by the grey line
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation observation in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that for feasibility of numerical simulation they consider only a model of coherent errors, independent among every time evolution operation, covering noise in the Rabi frequencies and detunings and position perturbations of each atom, and that they ignore the infidelity of single-qubit gates.
quotes: For feasibility of numerical simulation, we only consider a model of coherent errors independent among every time evolution operation that captures noise in the Rabi frequencies and detunings as well as position perturbations of each atom.
In this work, we ignore the infidelity of single-qubit gates as they generally have much higher fidelity than multiqubit gates
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own noise-model scope, Section II.
assertions.reader_inference: Incoherent error sources are outside the study, so the robustness result does not cover them.

papers.title_in_file: Applications of Quantum Machine Learning for Quantitative Finance
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2405.10119v1 (16 May 2024); matches the record's title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions, and the fraud detection and anomaly detection passages of the literature review (section 5.4 area).
papers.what_it_is: A review of quantum machine learning applications in quantitative finance, covering portfolio optimization, market prediction, pricing, risk management and fraud detection.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work gives an extensive overview of QML's uses in quantitative finance.
quotes: This work gives an extensive overview of QML's uses in quantitative finance, an important discipline in the financial industry.
assertions.certainty_reason: The review's statement of its own scope, Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The paper reports, citing other work, that simulations with registers up to 20 qubits showed quantum kernels with re-uploading had better average precision, and that at 20 qubits the quantum-classical separation of average precision was equal to 15%.
assertions.anchor: Section 5.4 anomaly detection passage (credit card fraud dataset)
quotes: Simulations with registers up to 20 qubits showed that quantum kernels with re-uploading demonstrated better average precision, with the advantage increasing with system size. At 20 qubits, the quantum-classical separation of average precision was equal to 15%.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the review attributes to another study.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is from simulation, not hardware.

assertions.value: The paper reports, citing other work, that on one dataset QSVM was found to perform better than the other methods in speed and accuracy, while on a second dataset its detection accuracy was comparable to that of the others.
quotes: With the former dataset, the QSVM was found to perform better than the others in terms of speed and accuracy; however, with the latter dataset, its detection accuracy was comparable to that of the others.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the review attributes to another study.
assertions.reader_inference: The two datasets are a bank loan dataset and an Israel credit card transactions dataset, named in the preceding sentence.

assertions.value: The authors state that, despite promising advancements and competitive performance of QML algorithms, challenges such as scalability, hardware limitations and algorithmic complexity remain.
quotes: Despite the promising advancements and competitive performance demonstrated by QML algorithms, challenges such as scalability, hardware limitations, and algorithmic complexity remain.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Resource frugal optimizer for quantum machine learning
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2211.04965v3 (28 Jul 2023); matches the record's title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section IV unbiased estimators (skimmed), convergence proposition in the appendix, numerical results figure captions, and discussion.
papers.what_it_is: A shot-frugal stochastic gradient descent optimizer (Refoqus) for variational QML that samples over both the dataset and the measurement operators.

assertions.value: The authors report that their numerics indicate Refoqus can save several orders of magnitude in shot cost, even relative to optimizers that sample over measurement operators alone.
quotes: Our numerics indicate that Refoqus can save several orders of magnitude in shot cost, even relative to optimizers that sample over measurement operators alone.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical experiments in one study.

assertions.value: The paper states that, provided the loss function satisfies the stated assumptions, the stochastic gradient descent routine used in Refoqus achieves geometric convergence to the optimal value of the cost function.
quotes: Proposition 4. Provided the loss function satisfies the assumptions stated below the stochastic gradient descent routine used in Refoqus achieves geometric convergence to the optimal value of the cost function.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposition 4 in the appendix, which reuses the gCANS convergence argument under stated assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The guarantee holds only under the assumptions the paper lists, which the reader did not check.

assertions.value: The authors state that they applied Refoqus only to a quantum PCA task and a quantum autoencoder task, that they expect similar results for other problems fitting their framework, and that applying the optimizer to a problem of interest on a real device is a next step.
quotes: Although we only applied Refoqus to a quantum PCA task and a quantum autoencoder task, we expect similar results to hold for other problems fitting our framework.
Furthermore, applying our optimizer to a problem of interest on a real device is an interesting and logical next step.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of the scope of testing, Section VIII.
assertions.reader_inference: The expectation for other problems is untested by the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Applicability of Measurement-based Quantum Computation towards Physically-driven Variational Quantum Eigensolver
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2307.10324v3 (26 Jul 2024); matches the record's title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusion and discussion. Numerical sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A proposal of a measurement-based Hamiltonian variational ansatz (MBHVA) for many-body simulation, tested numerically on the Heisenberg model and the Fermi-Hubbard chain.

assertions.value: The authors report from numerical experiments that MBHVA can have similar performance as circuit-based ansatz and is expected to reduce operation counts during execution compared to quantum circuits.
quotes: Numerical experiments show that MBHVA can have similar performance as circuit-based ansatz, and is expected to reduce operation counts during execution compared to quantum circuits, bringing the advantage of running time.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The operation-count advantage is stated for large multi-qubit rotations only.

assertions.value: The authors state that they did not consider the impact of errors in either system.
quotes: It should be emphasized that in our study, we did not consider the impact of errors in either system.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that their work is a theoretical analysis based on the CZ entanglement scheme and does not involve specific measurement methods for physical platforms.
quotes: Furthermore, our work is a theoretical analysis based on the CZ entanglement scheme and does not involve specific measurement methods for physical platforms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Section 4.

papers.title_in_file: Integrated error-suppressed pipeline for quantum optimization of nontrivial binary combinatorial optimization problems on gate-model hardware at the 156-qubit scale
papers.version_note: The file name uses the earlier title (127-qubit); the content is arXiv 2406.01743v5 (2 Mar 2026), retitled as in the record. Same paper, later version.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusion and the comment on recent experimental demonstrations. Methods and appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: A vendor (Q-CTRL) paper on a hybrid variational optimization pipeline for binary optimization on IBM gate-model hardware at the 156-qubit scale, compared with a classical solver and published annealer and trapped-ion results.

assertions.value: The authors report that for Max-Cut on random regular graphs with topologies not matched to device connectivity, the method achieves approximation ratios of 100% for unweighted 3-regular graphs up to 156 nodes, weighted regular graphs up to 80 nodes, and weighted 7-regular graphs up 50 nodes.
quotes: the method achieves approximation ratios of 100% for unweighted 3-regular graphs up to 156 nodes, weighted regular graphs up to 80 nodes, and weighted 7-regular graphs up 50 nodes.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical hardware result reported by the vendor, from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Q-CTRL describes its own solver; no independent replication is given in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that without their integrated approach, standard circuit execution at scale produces output indistinguishable from random sampling, which they say establishes the necessity of each pipeline component.
quotes: Without this integrated approach, we show that standard circuit execution at scale produces output indistinguishable from random sampling, establishing the necessity of each pipeline component.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result reported by the vendor, from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not claim quantum advantage over, or even practical equivalence with, the classical CPLEX solver.
quotes: For the avoidance of any doubt we do not claim quantum advantage over or even practical equivalence with the highly efficient classical CPLEX solver.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section V.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not comment on the potential for different relative performance among gate-model machines should their quantum solver be implemented on alternative hardware.
quotes: First, we do not comment on the potential for different relative performance among gate-model machines should our quantum solver be implemented on alternative hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own qualification of their comparison, Section V.
assertions.reader_inference: The results are specific to the IBM hardware used.

papers.title_in_file: A quantum information theoretic analysis of reinforcement learning-assisted quantum architecture search
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2404.06174v3 (15 Aug 2024); matches the record's title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, contributions, and discussion. Analysis sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of reinforcement-learning-assisted quantum architecture search for the variational quantum state diagonalisation problem, analysed with entanglement and entropy measures.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study investigates RL-QAS for crafting ansatz tailored to the variational quantum state diagonalisation problem.
quotes: This study investigates RL-QAS for crafting ansatz tailored to the variational quantum state diagonalisation problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors report that the concurrence of the admissible ansatz ranges between an upper and a lower bound, which are independent of the initialisation of the weights of the deep-Q network.
quotes: We observe that the concurrence of the admissible ansatz ranges between an upper and lower bound, which are independent of the initialisation of the weights of the deep-Q network.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical numerical observation from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that they propose an entanglement enhancing block that adjusts the input state's concurrence, thereby enhancing the performance of the RL-agent by a factor of 2.
quotes: Specifically, we propose an entanglement enhancing block that adjusts the input state's concurrence thereby enhancing the performance of the RL-agent by a factor of 2.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical numerical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors point out that the phase transition point is problem-specific, and leave open whether the phase transition behavior holds for other classes of algorithms.
quotes: However, we point out that the phase transition point is problem-specific.
It would be interesting to see if the phase transition behavior still holds for other classes of algorithms, a problem we leave for future research.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Hamiltonian Embedding of Images for Data Reuploading Classifiers
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2407.14055v2 (1 Aug 2024); matches the record's title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, simulation experiments and results (text and table caption), and discussion. Circuit derivation sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A data reuploading quantum neural network with Hamiltonian image embedding, compared by simulation against a quantum convolutional neural network on image datasets, plus six proposed design principles.

assertions.value: The authors report that, through numerical experiments on image datasets including MNIST and FashionMNIST, their model outperforms the quantum convolutional neural network by a large margin.
quotes: Through numerical experiments on images datasets, including the famous MNIST and FashionMNIST datasets, we demonstrate that our model outperforms the quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN)
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their model does not provide speedups for either training or inference when compared to classical techniques, while it still outperforms the baseline QCNN model with different random initialisations and without extensive hyperparameter search.
quotes: Although our model does not provide speedups for either training or inference when compared to classical techniques, it still outperforms the baseline QCNN model with different random initialisations and without extensive hyperparameter search.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit on speedup, Section 3.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The outperformance half of the sentence is an empirical result and would be low on its own.

assertions.value: The authors state that both the baseline and the proposed model were trained with 20 different parameter initialisations for the Kaggle CT Medical Images dataset and a subset of the Sklearn Digits dataset, each for 500 iterations with the Adam optimiser.
quotes: Both the baseline and the proposed model were trained with 20 different parameter initialisations for the Kaggle CT Medical Images dataset and subset of the Sklearn Digits dataset, each for 500 iterations with the Adam optimiser [42].
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 3.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that their six proposed principles for designing quantum machine learning models are far from complete.
quotes: it should be noted that these six principles are far from complete.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section 4.
